message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: check attachment_id against ^[\w-]+$ before building the URL.
reason: Scheme and host come from the operator-configured Confluence URL; attachment_id only lands in the path on that same host, so it cannot redirect the request to another host or to cloud metadata. (Path tampering stays inside the Confluence API the caller is already authorized for.)

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: refuse absolute download URLs whose host differs from the configured Confluence host so the session's credentials are never sent elsewhere.
reason: download_url is not a tool argument: it is taken from the configured Confluence server's own attachment metadata response, and relative links are prefixed with the configured base URL. The model cannot choose it.

message: Tool input chooses the URL fetched by confluence_fetcher.confluence._session.get. Without an allowlist the agent can be made to call internal services (for example http://169.254.169.254 or localhost admin APIs).
fix: Optional hardening: only follow download links on the configured Confluence host.
reason: Same as F002: the URL comes from Confluence's attachment listing for content_id, not from the tool arguments; relative links are prefixed with the configured base URL.

title: Confluence upload_attachment(s) reads and uploads any local file chosen by the model
reason: file_path (and file_paths in upload_attachments) goes straight from the tool arguments to an open/upload with no base-directory check, unlike the download path which uses validate_safe_path. An injected instruction in a page or issue can make the agent upload ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials or the server's .env to a Confluence page the attacker can read.
fix: Call validate_safe_path(file_path, base_dir=<configured upload dir>) on every path before opening it, refuse symlinks, and make the upload directory an explicit operator setting.

title: Jira update_issue attachments argument uploads any local file
reason: Paths from the update_issue tool argument are opened and attached to the issue with no containment check, so a prompt injection can exfiltrate any file readable by the server process into a Jira issue.
fix: Validate each path with validate_safe_path against an operator-configured upload directory before upload_attachment opens it.

title: X-Atlassian-Jira-Url / X-Atlassian-Confluence-Url request headers set the upstream URL with no allowlist
reason: Any HTTP client of the server can send these headers with any token and the server immediately makes requests to that URL (validation call, then every tool call), e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ or internal admin services; error text is returned to the caller.
fix: Only accept header URLs that match an operator allowlist of Atlassian hosts (e.g. *.atlassian.net or configured DC URLs), require https, and block private/loopback/link-local addresses after DNS resolution.

title: HTTP transports bind 0.0.0.0 and unauthenticated requests fall back to the operator's global Atlassian credentials

evidence.quote: # Fallback to global fetcher if not in HTTP context or no user info

reason: In SSE/streamable-HTTP mode the server listens on all interfaces and a request with no Authorization header is served with the globally configured token, so anyone who can reach the port acts as the operator in Jira/Confluence and can use the local-file upload tools (M001/M002). Whether this matters depends on whether the port is reachable.
fix: Default to 127.0.0.1, and in HTTP mode require per-request authentication (or a shared server token) instead of falling back to global credentials.

title: Page and issue content is returned to the model unmarked
reason: Confluence pages, comments and Jira issues are written by many people and go straight into the model context; this is the path by which injected text reaches the file-upload tools above.
fix: Wrap returned content as untrusted data, and keep write/upload tools behind human approval or READ_ONLY_MODE when processing third-party content.
